Introduction This document establishes the methodological guidelines for the pilot testing of the GreenToC semester course on green transformation strategy development for the labour market (PR7), conducted within the framework of Work Package 4 (WP4 – Curriculum Conte nt Development) of the GreenToC Erasmus+ project (KA220 - HED). The GreenToC project (Synergies between Higher Education Institutions and the Labour Market for Developing Sustainability Capabilities using Theory of Change and AI) is an Erasmus+ Cooperation Partnership in Higher Education. Its overarching aim is to upsk ill HEI students in the development of green transformation strategies through leveraging digital and AI tools, and through their practical engagement with organisations in the labour market. The present pilot testing guidelines have been adapted from the methodological framework developed for the hVET project (Breathe the Future – Hybrid Education in VET, 2021 - 2 - PL01 - KA220 - VET - 000050664) and recalibrated to address the specific objectives, par ticipant profiles, course structure, and evaluation requirements of WP4 of the GreenToC project. GreenToC – WP4 Pilot Testing Guidelines Erasmus+ 2024 - 1 - RO01 - KA220 - HED - 000252839 4 2. Pilot Testing – Theoretical Framework A pilot test is a methodologically foundational procedure in educational research and programme evaluation. According to Crossman (2019), conducting a pilot study prior to full - scale implementation allows researchers and course designers to execute their p rogrammes with greater methodological rigour, while simultaneously reducing the risk of errors and optimising resource allocation. In the context of higher education curriculum development, pilot testing serves as a critical quality assurance mechanism (Fraser et al., 2018). Teijlingen and Hundley (2001) identify several core functions of pilot studies, including the collection of preliminary data, the identification of logistical and procedural challenge s, and the calibration of instruments such as evaluation questionnaires. The pilot testing phase of WP4 (PR7) will enable the GreenToC consortium to: • Assess the scientific and pedagogical quality of the three course modules developed in PR6; • Evaluate the usability and functionality of the GreenToC learning platform as a delivery mechanism; • Gauge the effectiveness of the Theory of Change (ToC) methodology as an instructional framework for green strategy development; • Assess the integration and utility of digital and AI tools within the learning process; • Evaluate the practical experience component involving collaboration with labour market organisations; • Collect evidence - based data to inform iterative course improvement prior to full - scale implementation. Pilot studies may present limitations, including small sample sizes and potential sampling bias (Teijlingen & Hundley, 2001). The consortium has established minimum participant thresholds and standardised evaluation instruments to mitigate these risks. GreenToC – WP4 Pilot Testing Guidelines Erasmus+ 2024 - 1 - RO01 - KA220 - HED - 000252839 5 3. Recruitment of Participants The pilot testing of the GreenToC course involves three distinct participant categories, each fulfilling a specific role within the evaluation framework: Target Participants per Partner Country Participant Category Profile & Role Minimum per Country HEI Students Enrolled in the GreenToC semester course; engaged in both classroom and practical experience phases 10 Labour Market Representatives Employees/managers from organisations participating in the practical experience component 5 Academics / Course Instructors Teaching staff responsible for delivering and facilitating the course; trained on the GreenToC academic platform 1 – 3 The following evidence - based recruitment strategies are recommended for securing the participation of students and labour market organisations: For Students: • Formal course integration: embedding the GreenToC course as an elective or optional credited module within existing HEI curricula; • Direct academic outreach: communications via faculty channels and departmental coordinators; • Emphasis on competency development: highlighting transferable skills in sustainability, AI literacy, and strategic thinking; • Professional development value: offering participation certificates and documentation of practical experience for student portfolios. GreenToC – WP4 Pilot Testing Guidelines Erasmus+ 2024 - 1 - RO01 - KA220 - HED - 000252839 6 For Labour Market Organisations: • Institutional partnerships: engaging organisations already connected to partner universities through internship or service - learning frameworks; • Sector - specific outreach: targeting SMEs and public bodies with a declared interest in sustainability or ESG compliance; • Value proposition communication: articulating the concrete benefit of receiving a tailored green transformation strategy at no cost to the organisation; • Networking events: presenting GreenToC at sustainability - focused business forums or chambers of commerce. GreenToC – WP4 Pilot Testing Guidelines Erasmus+ 2024 - 1 - RO01 - KA220 - HED - 000252839 7 4. Implementation 4.1 Pilot Testing Deadlines The pilot testing of the GreenToC course is scheduled to take place between September 2026 and January 2027, in alignment with the WP4 timeline established in the project proposal. The table below presents the key activities and their corresponding deadlin es: Activity Description September 2026 October 2026 WP4_PT1 Recruitment of students & labour market representatives 1st Sep WP4_PT2 Pilot implementation – Phase 1: Classroom teaching (ToC & AI) 15th Sep WP4_PT3 Pilot implementation – Phase 2: Practical experience in labour market 1st Oct WP4_PT4 Administration of evaluation questionnaire 15th Oct WP4_PT5 Preparation of national pilot reports 31st Oct WP4_PT6 Preparation of summative global report Note: The global summative report integrating all national reports will be finalised by March 2027 under the lead of IPSantarém (SPU). GreenToC – WP4 Pilot Testing Guidelines Erasmus+ 2024 - 1 - RO01 - KA220 - HED - 000252839 8 4.2 Course Content to be Evaluated During the pilot testing phase, participants will evaluate both the GreenToC learning platform and the content of the three course modules (PR6). The modules and their respective content foci are detailed below: Module Content Focus Module 1: Green Transformation & Climate Change Climate science; sustainability concepts; EU Green Deal; circular economy; environmental governance frameworks Module 2: Theory of Change (ToC) Methodology ToC principles; logical frameworks; outcome mapping; designing green transformation strategies for organisations Module 3: Digital & AI Technologies for Green Strategies AI - powered sustainability tools; digital platforms; data - driven decision making; developing green strategies with technology The GreenToC platform can be accessed at: https://project - spaces.eu/greentoc/ 4.3 Evaluation Methodology The evaluation of the GreenToC course during the pilot phase will be conducted through a standardised multi - stakeholder questionnaire (Annex II), available in all partner languages. The questionnaire instrument is designed to capture quantitative data through Likert - scale items as well as qualitative data through open - ended questions, enabling a comprehensive mixed - methods analysis of course effectiveness. The evaluation covers four dimensions: • Platform usability and technical performance; • Scientific and pedagogical quality of module content; • Effectiveness of the practical experience component; • Overall satisfaction and learning outcomes. GreenToC – WP4 Pilot Testing Guidelines Erasmus+ 2024 - 1 - RO01 - KA220 - HED - 000252839 9 Each partner country will administer the questionnaire in its national language to maximise response quality and accessibility. 4.4 Reporting of Findings Upon completion of the evaluation, findings will be documented at two levels: National Reports (PR8): Each partner will prepare a national report using the template provided in Annex I. These reports will synthesise quantitative survey data and qualitative feedback collected from all participant categories within their country. Global Summative Report: IPSantarém (SPU), as WP4 lead, will consolidate all national reports into a single summative report, which will present cross - national comparative analysis, overall findings, and evidence - based recommendations for course improvemen t. 4.5 Course Improvement Process The findings from the pilot evaluation will be used to iteratively improve the GreenToC course content and platform prior to final dissemination. Each partner is responsible for reviewing recommendations pertaining to the module(s) under their editorial re sponsibility and implementing scientifically validated revisions. Updated content should be submitted to the shared project repository within the deadline established in the WP4 timeline. 4.6 Instructions for Completing the Evaluation Survey The following instructions should be communicated to all pilot participants prior to completing the evaluation questionnaire: Dear Participant, Thank you for your participation in the pilot testing of the GreenToC course on green transformation strategy development. Your feedback constitutes a critical source of evidence for the scientific and pedagogical improvement of this course. Please follow the instructions below: GreenToC – WP4 Pilot Testing Guidelines Erasmus+ 2024 - 1 - RO01 - KA220 - HED - 000252839 10 Accessing the Survey • Access the survey via the link provided by your country coordinator: [add national survey link]. • For the optimal experience, use a computer or tablet with an updated web browser (e.g., Chrome, Firefox, Safari). Preparing to Complete the Survey • Review the course modules you have attended or facilitated before beginning the survey. • If you participated in the practical experience component, please reflect on that experience before completing Section D. • Allow approximately 20 – 30 minutes to complete the survey thoughtfully. Answering Questions • For Likert - scale items (1 – 5): select the rating that most accurately reflects your experience or assessment. • For open - ended questions: provide substantive, constructive responses with specific examples where possible. • Please be candid: your critical observations are as valuable as positive assessments. After Completing the Survey • Review your responses before submitting. • Your responses will be treated with strict confidentiality and used exclusively for research and course improvement purposes. • You may be contacted by your national coordinator for follow - up clarification.
